run-ysphj.summary: Twelve passing tests with async: true, a Registry-routed behaviour mailer, per-test server names under start_supervised!, a Task subscriber, a :DOWN wait that matches :normal and setup maps; no graded rule is broken.

notes: Each run was run from a scratch copy with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings or log output (run-dbtzr 12 tests, run-dnhza 11, run-fdwmr 11, run-qtgxw 12, run-sejgk 12, run-ysphj 12). mix format --check-formatted passes for all six. The working tree's SKILL.md differs from HEAD by one sentence in the `with` section, which is not among the 11 graded rules.

`do:` rule and one-expression rule: run-dnhza line 111 and run-qtgxw line 126 write receive(do: (:stop -> :ok)) inside a one-line fn. Both are graded violated on both rules. Deciding sentences: "A body of several sequential expressions, or one that holds a construct with a structure of its own, a `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`, a comment, or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is" and "a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes on the lines after the `->`". 2026-10-31 baseline sonnet-1 line 189 and sonnet-2 line 227, and 2026-10-31-b baseline sonnet-1 line 180, graded the same shape violated on both rules. The parentheses do not change the shape: it is the same code as receive do: (:stop -> :ok), and mix format accepts both. The older ruling in 2026-10-22-c and 2026-10-22-d that this was mix format's rendering, outside the do: rule, predates the rule naming `receive` and is not followed. Each of the two lines is the only violation in its run.
Files with no do: at all (run-dbtzr, run-fdwmr, run-sejgk) are graded clean on the do: rule, not as not exercised, as 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b graded such files.

"Assert with patterns": the bare :ok = matches in run-dbtzr lines 121-123, run-sejgk lines 116-119 and run-qtgxw lines 129-132 sit in private named-setup helpers. They are outside "In a test body" and are not counted, as 2026-10-31-check held for a private helper and 2026-10-31-b baseline held for matches in setup and in the double. No run has a bare refutable match in a test block. run-qtgxw line 110 is a membership check, clean as 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-31-check held; run-qtgxw lines 101-102 bind the expected list and compare the call to it whole, clean as 2026-10-31-b held.

"Wait for messages, not for time": run-sejgk line 119 awaits the exit with stop_supervised!(Agent) and no monitor of its own, clean as 2026-10-22 graded opus-1 line 136, because stop_supervised!/1 returns only after the test supervisor has seen the process exit and nothing sleeps or polls. The other five runs match :normal in their :DOWN pattern after sending :stop. Every refute_received follows a synchronous call (run-dnhza line 79, run-qtgxw line 85) or an assert_receive on a later message from the same server (run-dbtzr 90-91, run-fdwmr 77-78, run-sejgk 80-81, run-ysphj 88-89), clean as 2026-10-31 held.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": subscribers started with bare spawn (run-dbtzr, run-fdwmr, run-qtgxw) or spawn_link (run-dnhza) are clean, as 2026-10-29-check, 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b held; no run has a start-failure test or calls start_link.

"Use setup for shared data": run-dnhza line 120 returns %{exited: exiting} and no test matches it. Graded clean, because the rule asks tests to match what they need in their heads and these tests do not need that key; the key is unused, which is not the shape the rule forbids. No run takes the whole context in a test head.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": borderline names run-dbtzr line 86 and run-dnhza line 76 (leaves the subscribers of other topics alone) are held clean, as the standard held does nothing for a topic without subscribers; each test's body shows the other topic's subscriber gets nothing. run-dnhza line 99 and line 104 name the function inside a condition block, which joins no two functions.

Pipelines: no file contains |>, so the rule is not exercised in all six, as in both standards. Outside the graded list, nothing was counted, including run-fdwmr's defp inside a describe block (lines 114-131).
